subject: Measurement specs, prompt samples and next steps for perf qualification
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@acme.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: perf targets and benchmark scope

Hi Stephanie — great call today, thanks for walking us through Redwood's Dedicated option. Quick recap + asks so we can scope the internal benchmark run: 

- Latency SLO: target p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 250ms for typical user flows (single prompt, median output length ~ 60 tokens). Please confirm whether your measurement should include network RTT or if we should supply a local measurement agent.
- Throughput & concurrency: we expect to sustain 200 qps for short queries with bursts to 400 qps for 30s; typical concurrent streams ~ 40 live streaming clients.
- Streaming behavior: streaming chunk size ~ 32 tokens; we need tail-latency (first-token and last-token) measurements as part of the report.
- Reproducibility: we want a repeatable harness with a fixed seed, warmup, and a reproducible prompt set. We can provide a representative sample of prompts and expected metrics.

Can you share Redwood's measurement template and the eval harness integration points (CLI or Docker image)? Also please confirm the exact definitions you use for p50/p95/p99 and whether tokenization (byte-pair) timing is included.

I've attached a first-pass prompt set (acme_prompt_samples_v1.jsonl) — it's intentionally mixed lengths and includes streaming-oriented inputs. Next step from our side: procurement will request the Detailed Statement of Work once we confirm benchmarks and SLAs.

Thanks,
Tom
COO, Acme AI
(Attachment: acme_prompt_samples_v1.jsonl - application/jsonl)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@acme.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-04T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: perf targets and benchmark scope

Hi Tom — thanks for the prompt set and clear summary. We're aligned on scope; a few clarifications and I'm attaching our measurement template.

1) Measurement boundaries: Our standard report includes server-side timing (inference start -> inference end), plus optional client-side RTT if you run the local probe. For baseline comparisons we report both server-only and end-to-end when the probe is present.

2) p50/p95/p99 definitions: percentiles computed over per-request end-to-end latency, measured in milliseconds. For streaming, we report: 
   - first-token latency (time from request sent to first token emitted)
   - inter-token mean latency (average time between token emissions)
   - last-token latency (time to final token)

3) Throughput profile: we'll run sustained runs at your requested qps (200) with 5-minute ramps and 30-minute steady-state windows; bursts to 400 qps are executed as 60s stress windows. We include a warmup period (10 minutes) and generate pre-warm KV cache profiles if you want cached vs cold-start comparisons.

4) Reproducibility: our harness supports fixed seeds for sampling and a recorded request replay mode. We need the following from you: tokenization config you want (BPE model name), typical input length distribution, and the sample set (you already provided).

Attaching: redwood_measurement_template.xlsx (includes exact metric definitions, run cadence, and CSV schemas for results).

Next steps: Marcus will follow up with the run orchestration details and the container image for the harness. Can we lock a 2-hour window next Tue (2027-03-09) for a joint smoke run?

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_measurement_template.xlsx - application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@acme.ai>; Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-04T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: perf targets and benchmark scope

Tom / Stephanie — quick tech notes to ensure our runs are reproducible and capture the metrics you care about. A few concrete configs we plan to use: 

- Warmup: 10 minutes of gradually increasing qps, followed by a 5-minute cooldown before steady-state. This eliminates JIT/compilation artifacts.
- Batch sizing: dynamic batching up to 16 tokens or up to 32 micro-batches depending on model memory pressure; we'll report effective batch sizes in the results.
- KV cache: we'll run both "cold" (empty KV) and "warm" (pre-loaded with 1k recent histories) passes — results will be labeled accordingly.
- Streaming semantics: harness will emulate streaming clients by opening a streaming session and sending the prompt once; chunking is controlled by max_chunk_tokens=32 and flush_on_eod=true. We'll measure first-token, mean inter-token, and tail percentiles.
- Tokenization: please confirm you want us to use the "acme-bpe-v1" tokenizer; otherwise we'll default to GPT-style BPE. Tokenization timing is included only where the local probe reports it — server-side tokenization time is measured separately.

Repro steps (what we'll share as a runnable artifact): 
- Docker image: redwood/bench-harness:v1.7 (invoked with --seed, --qps, --duration, --tokenizer args)
- Command example: docker run --rm redwood/bench-harness:v1.7 --config /configs/acme.json --seed 42 --qps 200 --duration 1800
- Output: CSV with per-request latency, per-token timings, and aggregated percentile reports; JSON summary for CI ingestion.

We will also produce a small reproducibility README with exact container hash and input sample set. If you want us to preserve the run artifacts (logs/trace) behind an access-controlled link for audit, we can stage them in a shared Drive folder.

Two quick questions that affect sizing: typical sequence lengths (prompt + response) for your interactive flows, and whether you expect multi-turn state to be loaded into KV per request.

I'll prepare the harness image and share the invocation scripts by EOD tomorrow.

—Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this looks excellent. Confirming: 

- Sequence lengths:  prompt median 40 tokens, response median 60 tokens, long-tail up to 512 tokens for batch jobs.
- KV usage: interactive flows use per-session KV of ~6 recent turns; we'll want the warm KV pass.
- Tokenizer: please use acme-bpe-v1 (attached in the sample archive).

I've uploaded a slightly expanded prompt set (acme_prompt_samples_v1b.jsonl) to the Drive link you provided and copied procurement on the thread for the SOW.
